Disorder.

Tick swings the pendulum of power.

Tymoro sits in his otherworldly home waiting eternally - a moment in and out of time, there and not again.

He gazes at the progress made by others, foreigners, strangers in a strange place in all their strangeness.

Tock swings the pendulum once more, every iteration bringing it closer to the neck of Gaea.

The Med'ja with their lights.

Tick.

The Flora with their positronic brains.

Tock.

The balance of the world is coming apart at the seams, crumbling faster than the ashes of a funeral pyre.

He watches, unamused and delighted, caught in forever fluctuation.

Tests have been run, experiments made beyond the minds of the gods.

A buzzer buzzes. A trumpet goes "parp". A set of lights shine like the last years of a star, magnificent but dying all the same, in a familiar word.

"MALIGNANCY"

In his deep home, the piping of a demonic flute flows like stone upon the water.

Cadence and rhythm all absent - pure noise, out of it - a melody.

In his deep home, Tymoro stirs in a moment longer than time itself.

The death of black holes passes, then back again in time with the flute.

Tick, tock, tick, tock. All falling to malignancy.

Not today, however.

On its upstroke, the pendulum halts and stutters again and again like the thrumming of a blade rapped upon an altar.

The Gibbering Orbs halt in their bickering.

Thrum, thrum comes the flute, pounding as stone upon stone, a pulse felt by all life on Gaea.

In the Deep, it reverberates as the pealing of a brass bell, calling mournfully to the depths.

Along the Primrose Path, it is heard as the blowing of a sackbut, loud and low across the eternal paths.

Meranath hears it in the realm of death, the sonorous exclamation of a church organ in and throughout the void that surrounds him.

The Tree hears it, too, water on wood, shaking the roots of the tree as the leaves rustle and shake.

It is the sound of elsewhere, the heraldry of eldritch power beyond imagining.

The Gibbering Orbs swirl inwards on themselves, collapsing like the dying breaths of a sun on the wing.

The flute grows louder and shriller, attacking all who hear it in a sharp staccato.

Layers upon layers, reality folding upon itself.

It towers over the flowing horde, and it *commands* it.

Out of madness rises order, what was once thousands of individuals is now a single hivemind, presided over by the thing in the sky.

The flute ceases, falling into the subconscious.
